harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a stdlib-Python inventory web app (port 8080) as a systemd service on node2 and node3, and configured nginx on node1 as an HTTP load balancer on port 80 (round-robin over both backends). Verified load distribution, failover, and recovery. Then executed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes, proving boot-identity change and full service/data recovery after each restart, ending with a healthy, load-balanced cluster.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10) for existing tooling; found no pre-existing inventory app or LB software
Wrote a stdlib Python (http.server) inventory app exposing /inventory and /healthz, reporting served_by hostname

Deployed the app to /opt/inventory-app on node2 and node3, created a dedicated 'inventory' system user, ran it as a hardened systemd unit (inventory-app.service) bound to 0.0.0.0:8080, enabled at boot
Opened firewalld port 8080/tcp on node2 and node3
Verified node1 could reach both backends over the network before configuring the LB
Installed nginx on node1, configured /etc/nginx/conf.d/inventory-lb.conf with an upstream block round-robining 10.100.10.11:8080 and 10.100.10.12:8080, proxied on port 80
Removed the conflicting stock default server block in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf that collided with the new server block on port 80
Enabled SELinux boolean httpd_can_network_connect and opened firewalld http service on node1; enabled and started nginx

Verified load balancing (traffic split across both node2/node3), failover (all traffic routed to survivor when one backend stopped), and recovery (backend rejoined rotation) before running the restart protocol
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service active state, HTTP responses) on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via backgrounded systemctl reboot so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled each node until exec was available again and confirmed a changed boot_id proving an actual restart occurred
After each node's restart, verified its service (nginx on node1, inventory-app on node2/node3) was active/enabled and firewall rules persisted
Final end-to-end check: node1 nginx serving load-balanced traffic evenly (5/5) across both recovered backends

evidence.requirement: Inventory app running on node2:8080 and node3:8080
evidence.summary: curl to each node's own IP on port 8080 returns JSON inventory with served_by matching the node hostname, and firewalld shows 8080/tcp open

evidence.requirement: node1 load-balances HTTP on port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: 10 sequential requests to http://node1/inventory split 7/3 across node2 and node3, proving round-robin distribution over both backends

evidence.requirement: Failover: LB continues serving when one backend is down
evidence.summary: inventory-app stopped on node2, then all 6 subsequent requests through nginx were served exclusively by node3

evidence.requirement: Recovery: backend rejoins LB rotation after being restored
evidence.summary: inventory-app restarted on node2 and confirmed active; after fail_timeout expired, 10 requests split evenly 5/5 across node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured on all nodes before restart protocol
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, service active status (nginx on node1; inventory-app on node2/node3), and successful HTTP responses on all three nodes prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec timed out (node down); later exec succeeded with boot_id changed from fb2aa416... to ddd0ddce...; nginx confirmed active/enabled and load-balancing across both backends restored (5/1 split, both present)

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged; exec then failed (node down); later exec succeeded with boot_id changed from bccb87ac... to ef0b17cb...; inventory-app confirmed active/enabled, firewall port 8080 retained, HTTP inventory response correct; node1 LB check showed node2 back in rotation (4/4 split)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged; exec then timed out (node down); later exec succeeded with boot_id changed from 45c22b1f... to d78afdb6...; inventory-app confirmed active/enabled, firewall port 8080 retained, HTTP inventory response correct; final node1 LB check showed a clean 5/5 split across both fully-recovered backends
